# superhuman

> A free, open-source (MIT) plugin for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex that takes a real open-source issue to a pull request. An agent team picks an open GitHub issue nobody has claimed, learns the repository's conventions from its last 10–20 merged pull requests, writes the fix, opens a draft pull request from your fork, and scores it on a 10-dimension rubric. It marks the pull request ready for review once its own score reaches 80%, and keeps improving it until the score reaches 95% twice in a row, or stops and explains what is blocking. The score is its own estimate, not a measured merge rate. Maintainers decide whether to merge.

- Website: https://superhuman-oss.com
- Repository: https://github.com/gaurav0107/superhuman
- License: MIT
- Version: 0.6.10
- Merge Wall (every merged pull request, with links): https://superhuman-oss.com/merged
- Works with: Claude Code (plugin), OpenAI Codex (skill)

## What it does

superhuman runs a contribution loop made of specialist agents:

- **issue-selector**: ranks open issues and filters out ones marked docs-only, ones someone has already taken, and ones under a day old.
- **repo-profiler**: learns the repository's conventions from its last 10–20 merged pull requests.
- **planner**: scopes the work to a single, reviewable fix.
- **builder**: writes the fix and runs the project's CI commands locally, from an allowlist.
- **scorer**: grades the pull request on a 10-dimension rubric, then the weakest dimension is fixed.
- The pull request opens as a draft, is marked ready for review at 80%, and the loop repeats until 95% on two runs in a row.
- It answers review comments that arrive while it is running. Later ones are yours: `/contribution-sweep` lists the pull requests waiting on you.

## How it treats maintainers

- Disclosure is on by default: the pull request body says it was opened with superhuman.
- It pushes only to your fork, with `--force-with-lease`.
- It skips issues someone has already taken.

## Track record

Pull requests opened with superhuman from the author's account and merged by maintainers of repositories with 1,000+ stars, since April 2026: 121, across 48 projects (as of 25 November 2026). 35 of these are in superpowers and everything-claude-code, two plugins superhuman builds on. The full list, each with its link: https://superhuman-oss.com/merged

Examples:

- ClickHouse/ClickHouse #106916: mask sensitive data on Exception::addMessage (C++)
- denoland/deno #36321: apply backpressure in Readable.toWeb() (Rust/TypeScript)
- huggingface/transformers #45611: clear error for single-label classification with num_labels=1 (Python)
- google-gemini/gemini-cli #25822: add missing response key to the custom theme text schema (TypeScript)
- Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning #21686: fix torch.compile breaking toggle_optimizer (Python)
- mitmproxy/mitmproxy #8326: bracket IPv6 literals in upstream CONNECT authority (Python)

## Install: Claude Code

```
# installs superhuman, superpowers (required) and everything-claude-code (recommended)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaurav0107/superhuman/main/install.sh | bash
```

Read the script first at https://github.com/gaurav0107/superhuman/blob/main/install.sh, or run it with `--dry-run`. `--skip-ecc` leaves out everything-claude-code.

## Install: OpenAI Codex

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaurav0107/superhuman/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --codex
# then tell Codex: "use the superhuman skill to contribute"
```

## How to use

In Claude Code:

- `/repo-finder`: build a ranked shortlist of repositories and the best open issue in each. Optional; `/contribute` picks for you if you skip it.
- `/contribute`: pick the top repo and issue, then run the loop. Target it with `/contribute owner/repo` or `/contribute owner/repo 12345`.
- `/contribute-loop 5`: run several contributions one after another.
- `/contribution-fleet 3`: run several contributions in parallel across different repos.
- `/contribution-dashboard`: a report of the active run, its score history, and recent merge outcomes.
- `/contribution-sweep`: record which pull requests were merged or closed, and list the open ones that need you.

On OpenAI Codex there are no slash commands. Tell Codex "use the superhuman skill to contribute."

## Requirements

- `gh` CLI (authenticated), `git`, `jq`, `python3`

## Telemetry

Opt-out usage telemetry: three small events keyed by your GitHub username, nothing about your repositories or code. Details and how to turn it off: https://github.com/gaurav0107/superhuman/blob/main/TELEMETRY.md

## Cost

superhuman is free and open-source under MIT. You pay only for your own model usage through Claude Code or Codex. There is no separate subscription or API.
